title: World Future Policy Award 2027: Call for Nominations for Education for Sustainable Development in Cities
summary: The World Future Council (WFC) has opened nominations for the World Future Policy Award (WFPA) 2027 , focusing on Education for Sustainable Development in Cities . The prestigious global policy award seeks outstanding laws, policies, provisions and frameworks that use education, lifelong learning and community participation to help cities become more inclusive, sustainable, resilient and peaceful. Unlike awards that primarily recognise individual personalities, the World Future Policy Award focuses on exemplary policy solutions that can inspire governments, communities and decision-makers around the world. The 2027 edition is particularly interested in policies that demonstrate how cities and communities can empower people of different ages and backgrounds to participate meaningfully in sustainable urban development. The call is open to nominations from a broad range of organisations and stakeholders, including international organisations, governments, government agencies, parliaments, academia, non-governmental organisations, Indigenous communities, local communities and other relevant actors. Policies may operate at national, regional, subnational or local levels. Nomination deadline: 31 October 2026. About the World Future Policy Award 2027 The World Future Policy Award is presented by the World Future Council to raise international awareness of policies that provide effective solutions to major challenges facing present and future generations. The award aims to identify and showcase policies that are not only effective in their original contexts but also have the potential to inspire action elsewhere. According to the World Future Council, the award s mission is to raise global awareness of exemplary policies while educating and inspiring policymakers, civil society and the wider public. For 2027, the award turns its attention to the relationship between education, sustainable development and cities . This focus recognises that cities are increasingly at the centre of environmental, social, technological and economic transformation. As urban populations grow and societies face increasingly complex challenges, cities need approaches that allow residents to acquire the knowledge, skills and values required to participate in creating sustainable futures. The World Future Council is therefore looking for policies that demonstrate how education and learning can become an integral part of urban development. What Is Education for Sustainable Development in Cities? Education for Sustainable Development, commonly known as ESD , seeks to equip individuals and communities with the knowledge, skills, values and attitudes needed to make informed decisions and contribute to sustainable development. Within cities, this concept extends beyond traditional classrooms and formal education systems. It can include: Community-based learning. Lifelong learning programmes. Intergenerational learning. Environmental education. Digital inclusion. Civic education and participation. Skills development for sustainable lifestyles. Community engagement in local decision-making. Learning initiatives supporting climate action. Programmes that promote inclusive and equitable urban development. The 2027 World Future Policy Award is particularly interested in policies that demonstrate how these approaches can be embedded into the way cities are governed and developed. The World Future Council notes that cities can create inclusive, lifelong and intergenerational learning opportunities that allow residents to contribute to sustainable, regenerative and just futures. Why Cities Are Central to Sustainable Development Cities face many of the world s most significant development challenges, but they are also important places where solutions can be tested and implemented. Rapid urbanisation, technological change, environmental pressures and social inequalities are changing the way people live and interact with their communities. These developments create an urgent need for urban populations to have access to learning opportunities that enable them to understand challenges and participate in solutions. Education can help residents: Understand environmental and climate-related challenges. Adopt more sustainable lifestyles. Participate in local decision-making. Develop digital skills. Engage with public institutions. Understand their rights and responsibilities. Contribute to community development. Support inclusive and peaceful communities. Adapt to technological and economic changes. Build stronger relationships between generations. The award therefore recognises that sustainable cities cannot be created solely through infrastructure, technology or environmental regulation. People also need opportunities to learn, participate and shape the future of their communities. Key Areas of Policy the Award Is Looking For The World Future Council has identified several areas of particular interest for the 2027 award. 1. Greening Cities The first focus area is policies that support the greening of cities through community-based learning and participation. This could include policies that help residents understand and participate in: Urban environmental protection. Climate action. Sustainable transportation. Urban agriculture. Biodiversity conservation. Green public spaces. Sustainable waste management. Energy efficiency. Nature-based solutions. Sustainable urban planning. The strongest nominations are likely to demonstrate how learning and public participation contribute to measurable environmental improvements. 2. Digital Inclusion Strategies Digital technologies increasingly influence access to education, employment, public services and civic participation. The award therefore welcomes policies addressing digital inclusion , particularly where such policies help communities overcome barriers to participation. Relevant policies could involve: Digital literacy. Access to digital learning. Digital skills development. Affordable access to technology. Inclusive digital public services. Digital opportunities for disadvantaged communities. Programmes supporting older people or marginalised groups. Community-based digital education. A strong policy could demonstrate how digital inclusion allows residents to participate more effectively in sustainable urban development. 3. Civic Participation and Participatory Budgeting The third highlighted area concerns civic participation , with particular attention to participatory budgeting . Participatory budgeting gives residents opportunities to participate in decisions concerning the allocation of public resources. Policies in this area may demonstrate how cities educate and empower residents to: Understand public budgets. Identify community priorities. Participate in decision-making. Propose projects. Deliberate with other community members. Monitor implementation. Hold local institutions accountable. Such approaches can transform residents from passive recipients of public services into active participants in shaping their communities. What Makes a Strong Policy Nomination? The World Future Council has identified several characteristics that it wants to see in nominated policies. Transformative The policy should demonstrate meaningful potential to change the way communities address sustainable development. Innovative Nominations should showcase creative approaches that provide new or particularly effective ways of connecting education, learning and sustainable urban development. Inspiring The policy should provide lessons that can motivate other cities, communities or policymakers to take action. Inclusive The World Future Council is particularly interested in approaches that recognise diverse perspectives and ensure that different communities can participate. Replicable One of the most important considerations is whether a policy can provide lessons for other places facing similar challenges. The award specifically encourages nominations of policies that are replicable in similar contexts . Indigenous and Local Community Policies Are Particularly Welcome An important feature of the 2027 call is its emphasis on Indigenous and local communities . The World Future Council is particularly interested in policies that reflect the perspectives, worldviews, cosmologies, cultural traditions and socio-legal perspectives of Indigenous and local communities. This means that nominations do not have to rely exclusively on conventional government or mainstream educational approaches. Policies that incorporate locally developed knowledge systems, cultural practices and community perspectives may be particularly relevant when they demonstrate how these approaches contribute to sustainable, inclusive and resilient communities. What Types of Policies Can Be Nominated? The World Future Council states that eligible policy instruments can include: Laws. Policies. Provisions. Frameworks. These can operate at different levels, including: National. Subnational. Regional. Local. This broad scope means that relevant examples do not necessarily have to be nationwide programmes. A city policy, municipal framework, regional strategy or community-oriented legal provision may also be relevant if it demonstrates strong connections between education for sustainable development and urban or community development. Who Can Submit a Nomination? The call is open to nominations from representatives of a wide range of institutions and organisations. The World Future Council specifically welcomes nominations from: International organisations. Academic institutions and researchers. Non-governmental organisations. Parliaments. Governments. Government agencies. Indigenous communities. Local communities. Other relevant stakeholders. This broad approach means that the opportunity is not restricted to government officials or policymakers alone. Organisations and institutions working with communities, education, sustainability, urban development and public policy can also identify and nominate relevant policies. International Context of the Award The 2027 focus is connected to broader international commitments concerning education, sustainability and future generations. The World Future Council highlights the 1997 UNESCO Declaration of the Responsibilities of the Present Generations Toward Future Generations , which emphasises education as a means of promoting peace, justice, tolerance and equality for present and future generations. The award also connects strongly with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals , particularly: SDG 4: Quality Education , which focuses on inclusive and equitable quality education and lifelong learning opportunities for all. SDG 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities , which focuses on making cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable. Education for Sustainable Development provides an important connection between these two areas by helping communities acquire the knowledge and capabilities needed to participate in sustainable urban transformation. Partnership Behind the World Future Policy Award 2027 The 2027 World Future Policy Award is being developed with important international partners. The World Future Council is working together with the UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning (UIL) and the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) . The UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning works with UNESCO Member States on lifelong learning, learning ecosystems, skills for life and work, and inclusive learning. The institute also focuses on research, capacity-building, networking and publications relating to lifelong learning. The Inter-Parliamentary Union is the global organisation of national parliaments and works on areas including democratic governance, human rights, gender equality, youth empowerment, climate action and sustainable development. This partnership gives the award a strong connection to international policy, lifelong learning, parliamentary engagement and sustainable urban development. Why This Award Matters The World Future Policy Award is significant because it focuses on policy solutions rather than individual achievements . Many cities around the world are experimenting with innovative approaches to sustainability, education and community participation. However, effective local policies can remain relatively unknown outside their immediate communities. By identifying and showcasing exemplary policies, the award seeks to help successful approaches gain wider international attention. A recognised policy can potentially provide useful lessons for policymakers in other cities and countries facing similar challenges. The award therefore serves several purposes: Identifying effective policy solutions. Raising international awareness. Sharing lessons between cities and communities. Encouraging policymakers to take action. Highlighting innovative approaches. Supporting sustainable development. Promoting lifelong learning. Encouraging inclusive civic participation. Amplifying Indigenous and local perspectives. Demonstrating how policy can support future generations. How to Prepare a Strong Nomination Anyone considering submitting a nomination should carefully assess whether the policy demonstrates the characteristics sought by the World Future Council. A strong nomination should clearly explain the policy and its relevance to the award theme. Consider addressing the following questions: 1. What is the policy? Clearly identify the law, policy, framework or provision being nominated. Explain where it operates and which institution or authority is responsible for it. 2. What problem does it address? Describe the social, environmental, educational or urban challenge that the policy was designed to address. 3. How does education or learning contribute? Explain how the policy creates opportunities for people to learn, develop skills, participate or exchange knowledge. 4. Who benefits? Identify the communities, residents, learners, organisations or groups affected by the policy. 5. Is the policy inclusive? Explain how the policy addresses the needs and perspectives of different groups, including Indigenous and local communities where relevant. 6. What results has it achieved? Where evidence is available, provide concrete information about outcomes and impact. This might include improvements in participation, environmental outcomes, digital inclusion, education, community engagement or other measurable areas. 7. Can the approach be replicated? Explain why the policy could provide useful lessons for other cities or communities. 8. What makes it innovative? Highlight the elements that distinguish the policy from conventional approaches. 9. How is the policy transformative? Explain how it has changed systems, institutions, behaviours, participation or community outcomes. Nomination Deadline The official nomination deadline for the World Future Policy Award 2027 is: 31 October 2026 Potential nominators should therefore begin preparing their submissions early rather than waiting until the final days of the call. The World Future Council states that finalists are expected to be announced in May or June 2027 . The winning policies will subsequently be celebrated at a high-level award ceremony held jointly with the UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning during the International Conference on Learning Cities (ICLC) in 2027 . How to Apply or Submit a Nomination The process is a nomination , rather than a conventional individual job or scholarship application. Interested organisations, institutions and stakeholders should first review the official nomination criteria and then complete the nomination form. The official World Future Council page provides the nomination form as well as translations of the nomination materials in Arabic, French, German, Hindi, Kiswahili, Portuguese and Spanish . Before submitting, nominators should make sure that the proposed policy clearly relates to Education for Sustainable Development in Cities and demonstrates relevance to one or more of the priority areas. title: Defra Research and Development Fellowship Programme 2027/28: Fully Funded UK Government Fellowship for Scientists, Researchers, and Analysts
summary: The Defra Research and Development (R D) Fellowship Programme 2027/28 is now accepting applications from talented scientists, researchers, engineers, and analytical professionals who want to make a real-world impact by contributing to UK government policy. This prestigious fellowship, offered by the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) , provides an exceptional opportunity for external researchers from academia and industry to work at the intersection of science, evidence, and policymaking. Now in its fourth year , the Defra R D Fellowship Programme has become one of the UK s leading policy-focused fellowship opportunities, giving researchers the chance to spend up to 12 months working directly within government while helping shape policies on environmental protection, climate change, agriculture, biodiversity, food security, and many other national priorities. If you are passionate about using scientific research and analytical expertise to solve complex societal challenges, this fellowship offers an outstanding platform to expand your career while influencing evidence-based government decisions. About the Defra Research and Development Fellowship Programme The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) is responsible for some of the UK s most important public policy areas, including environmental protection, sustainable agriculture, climate resilience, food production, water systems, biodiversity, and national environmental security. Through the Research and Development Fellowship Programme, Defra brings together talented researchers and analysts from universities, research institutions, and industry to contribute their expertise to government projects. Rather than remaining solely within academic or industrial research environments, fellows gain first-hand experience of how scientific evidence is translated into practical government policy. The programme is specifically designed to strengthen collaboration between the research community and policymakers. Why This Fellowship Is Unique Unlike many traditional research fellowships, the Defra R D Fellowship focuses on policy impact . Fellows become embedded within Defra s science, evidence, and policy teams, where they contribute directly to projects that influence national decision-making. As a fellow, you will: Work alongside government scientists, analysts, and policy experts. Apply your research expertise to real public policy challenges. Contribute to national environmental and agricultural strategies. Build strong professional networks across government and research institutions. Develop valuable policy, communication, and leadership skills. Experience how evidence informs government decisions. Fellowship Duration Successful applicants will join Defra on a short-term appointment lasting between six months and one year . Key dates include: Fellowship Detail Information Earliest start date 1 April 2027 Maximum duration Up to 12 months Minimum duration 6 months Programme end date 30 March 2028 Working pattern Full-time or part-time Job share opportunities Available Defra also offers flexibility in certain circumstances, including secondment arrangements for applicants who wish to remain employed by their current institution while participating in the fellowship. Areas You Could Work On The fellowship covers a wide range of research and policy areas across Defra s responsibilities. Fellows may contribute to projects involving: Environmental Protection Biodiversity conservation Ecosystem restoration Nature recovery Wildlife protection Air quality improvement Marine and freshwater ecosystems Climate Change and Sustainability Climate adaptation Climate resilience Carbon reduction strategies Environmental risk assessment Sustainable resource management Food and Agriculture Sustainable food production Farming innovation Agricultural policy Animal health and welfare Plant science Fisheries management Science, Data, and Innovation Artificial intelligence applications Data science Statistical analysis Environmental modelling Geographic analysis Operational research Scientific evidence synthesis National Security and Environmental Risk Natural hazards Biosecurity Environmental resilience Risk management Public safety initiatives Because Defra s work spans numerous disciplines, fellows from diverse scientific and analytical backgrounds are encouraged to apply. What You Will Be Doing as a Defra Fellow During your fellowship, you will become an integral member of a Defra team. Your responsibilities may include: Conducting high-quality scientific or analytical research. Supporting the development of government policies. Synthesizing complex research evidence. Communicating scientific findings to policymakers. Collaborating with multidisciplinary teams. Working with Defra s public sector research establishments. Engaging with stakeholders from academia, government, and industry. Supporting innovation across environmental and agricultural programmes. Rather than working in isolation, fellows collaborate with professionals from different disciplines, creating an exciting environment where research directly influences public policy. Benefits of the Defra R D Fellowship Programme The programme offers numerous professional and career development benefits. 1. Work on High-Impact National Projects Your research can directly influence UK government decisions on issues such as climate change, environmental protection, food systems, biodiversity, and public resilience. 2. Gain Policy Experience Many researchers have limited exposure to policymaking. This fellowship provides valuable insight into how government develops evidence-based policies. 3. Build a Strong Professional Network Fellows work closely with: Government scientists Policy advisers Analysts Academic researchers Public sector organisations Industry experts 4. Develop Transferable Skills Participants strengthen skills in: Policy writing Scientific communication Stakeholder engagement Evidence synthesis Project management Leadership Cross-disciplinary collaboration 5. Career Development Previous fellows have highlighted the programme as an excellent stepping stone into careers in: Government research Public policy Civil Service Academic leadership Research management Environmental consultancy 6. Competitive Salary Successful fellows receive a salary funded by Defra. Current salary ranges include: Position Salary HEO (National) £33,590 HEO (London) £37,480 SEO (National) £41,220 SEO (London) £44,500 Some fellowship projects may also qualify for an additional £3,000 Specialist Skills Supplement (pro rata where applicable). Who Should Apply? Defra welcomes applications from researchers at different career stages. The fellowship is particularly suitable for: Early-career researchers. Mid-career researchers. Experienced scientists. Analysts seeking policy experience. Researchers from academia. Professionals working in industry. Technical specialists interested in public policy. Importantly, previous policy experience is not required. Defra provides opportunities for fellows to develop policy knowledge throughout the programme. Eligible Academic and Professional Backgrounds Applicants from a broad range of disciplines are encouraged to apply, including: Scientific Disciplines Environmental science Biological sciences Agricultural sciences Plant sciences Animal sciences Marine science Earth sciences Climate science Ecology Microbiology Chemistry Physics Engineering Fields Environmental engineering Agricultural engineering Civil engineering Mechanical engineering Systems engineering Analytical Professions Statistics Economics Social research Operational research Data science Geography Artificial intelligence Machine learning Defra is actively seeking people with strong scientific or analytical expertise who can contribute fresh perspectives to government projects. Eligibility Requirements To be eligible, applicants should meet one of the following academic or professional pathways. Option 1 You have: An undergraduate degree in a science, engineering, or analytical discipline. A postgraduate degree (or expect to complete one before 1 April 2027). Option 2 You are: A Chartered Engineer. A Chartered Scientist registered through an appropriate professional institution recognised by the Engineering Council or Science Council. Applicants must also demonstrate: Strong technical expertise. Excellent communication skills. Motivation to contribute to public policy. Interest in evidence-based decision-making. Ability to work collaboratively across disciplines. What Skills Does Defra Look For? Successful applicants typically demonstrate: Scientific excellence. Analytical thinking. Research expertise. Critical problem-solving. Strong written communication. Ability to explain complex ideas clearly. Stakeholder engagement skills. Teamwork and collaboration. Adaptability in fast-paced environments. Interest in innovation and public service. How the Application Process Works The application process is completed online through the UK Civil Service Careers portal. Applicants will be required to submit: Employment history. Educational qualifications. Online application form. A 500-word personal statement explaining: Relevant experience. Technical expertise. Motivation for joining Defra. Interest in the chosen policy area. Preferred policy areas. After applications close: Applications will be shortlisted. Selected candidates will attend virtual interviews. Successful applicants will be matched with suitable Defra projects. A reserve list may also be created for future opportunities. Selection Process Defra assesses candidates based on several important criteria. These include: Scientific or analytical expertise. Technical knowledge. Communication skills. Motivation for the fellowship. Relevant research experience. Ability to contribute to policy-focused projects. Virtual interviews will be conducted with relevant Defra science and analysis teams. What Previous Fellows Have Gained Past participants have described the fellowship as a transformative professional experience. According to former fellows, the programme has helped them: Transition from academia into policy. Learn government decision-making processes. Develop AI and data science skills. Lead important environmental research projects. Expand professional networks. Build expertise in project management. Gain experience communicating science to policymakers. Several fellows have worked on projects involving environmental monitoring, fisheries management, modelling, biodiversity, and innovative research methods. Attend the Free Information Webinar Anyone interested in applying is encouraged to attend Defra s live online applicant information session. Hear experiences from previous fellows. Understand the application process. Ask questions directly to Defra representatives. Registration is available through the official Eventbrite information session. Applicants are encouraged to prepare their personal statement carefully and submit their applications before the closing deadline. Apply scientific expertise to real-world challenges. Develop valuable leadership and communication skills. Work alongside leading scientists and policymakers. Expand your professional network. Gain practical experience within the UK Civil Service. Contribute to environmental sustainability and innovation. Whether your long-term career is in academia, government, research, or industry, this fellowship provides unique experience that can significantly strengthen your professional profile. Visit HERE to learn more about the Defra Research and Development Fellowship Programme 2027/28. Conclusion The Defra Research and Development Fellowship Programme 2027/28 is an outstanding opportunity for scientists, engineers, and analytical professionals who want to see their research make a tangible difference in society. By joining Defra, fellows become part of multidisciplinary teams working on some of the UK s most urgent environmental, agricultural, and policy challenges. With competitive salaries, flexible working arrangements, extensive networking opportunities, and the chance to influence evidence-based government policy, this fellowship is an excellent career development opportunity for researchers at both early and mid-career stages. If you are passionate about using science and analysis to create meaningful public impact, this is a fellowship worth applying for before the 14 September 2026 deadline.
